sentences.text:
Facts of the present case are as follows:
The claimants/appellants are the owner of the land bearing Sy.No.82/3 of Kurikota village measuring 31 guntas Situated in district and taluk Gulbarga, was acquired by the State Government/respondents under preliminary notification dated 29.11.2001 for the purpose of construction of Gandori Nala project.
The Land Acquisition Officer by passed an award of Rs.23,100/- on 03.01.2004.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants filed protest petition under Section 18(1) of Land Acquisition Act , 1894 before the S.L.A.O.
The Reference NC: 2024:KHC-K:2166 Court considering the entire materials on record has proceeded to determine the market value at the rate of Rs.43,000/- per acre.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have filed LAC.A.No.635/2012 before IV Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Gulbarga.

entities.text: Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Gulbarga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: After hearing both sides learned District and Sessions judge vide order dated 06.11.2014 has allowed the appeal in part and awarded a compensation of Rs.1,76,200/- by condoning the delay of 2277 days in filing the appeal, denying interest for the belated period.
Hence, present appeal is filed for enhancement of the compensation.
3. Heard both parties.
4. Sri.
Harshvardhan.

R.Malipatil, learned counsel for the claimants submit that the impugned judgment and award passed by the First Appellate Court granting compensation of Rs.1,76,200/-
per acre for dry land is unreasonable and contrary to the materials on record and the same is liable to be modified.

He further submits that in respect of the property acquired in other cases of Afzalpur for the same project in the year 2006, this Court NC: 2024:KHC-K:2166 has fixed marked value of Rs.2,76,666/- per acre for dry land.
Therefore, the claimants are also entitled for the similar compensation after depreciation of 5%.
If 5% per acre is considered, the market value of the property in question would be Rs.2,07,499/- for dry land.

He would further contends that this Court in respect of the project notification issued in the year 2004 in MSA No.200119/2015, has determined the market value at the rate of Rs.2,50,000/- per acre for dry land with all statutory benefits.
Even if, 5% depreciation is considered the market value would still be Rs.2,00,000/- per acre.

He further submits that in MSA No.200008/2016 (LAC) dated 05.04.2018 Co-ordinate bench of this Court has determined the market value of the property at the rate of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre for the dry land.
Therefore, he sought for allowing this appeal by modifying the judgment and award passed by First Appellate Court.

5. Per contra, Sri.Sanjeev Kumar.C.Patil, learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 and Sri.Gopal Krishna.B.Yadav, learned HCGP for respondents No.3 and NC: 2024:KHC-K:2166 4 submit that in the absence of any material documents on record by the claimants, the judgment and award passed by the First Appellate Court is just and reasonable.

Learned counsel have not disputed the fact that Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in MSA No.200008/2016(LAC) in respect of the very same project and the same notification was issued in the year 2001 and awarded Rs.2,00,000/- per acre for dry land with all statutory benefits.

sentences.text: Having heard the parties, it is undisputed fact that the land of the claimants was acquired by the respondents for the purpose of construction of Gandori Nala Project by issuance of preliminary notification dated 29.11.2001.
The LAO fixed the market value at the rate of Rs.23,100/- per acre for the dry land.

After referring to the Reference Court, the compensation was enhanced as Rs.43,000/-
per acre.
The First Appellate Court on re-appreciation of the material on record awarded compensation of Rs.1,76,200/- per acre for dry land.

It is also not in dispute that Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has passed NC: 2024:KHC-K:2166 an award of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre to land acquired by the respondents pertaining to the same notification.
When the respondents have acquired the land of the farmers under the same notification for the same project, there should be uniformity of compensation.
Apart from this, the respondents have not challenged the order passed by Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in MSA No.200008/2016(LAC) dated 05.04.2018.

On examination of the materials placed before this Court is just and proper to award the compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre for the dry land as per the judgment of Co-ordinate bench of this Court.
7. In view of the aforesaid reasons, MSA is allowed in part with cost.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the First Appellate Court dated 06.11.2014 is LAC No.635/2012 is modified.
The claimants/appellants are entitled for a compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre for the dry land with all statutory benefits.

8. However, it is made clear that the claimants/appellants are not entitled for any interest for - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:2166 the delay occurred, either before the First Appellate Court or before this Court in the present appeal.

Accordingly, the appeal is disposed off. MSA No.200007/2016:
